reasons: Runs on its own and reports a clear pass or fail.
Covers basis tags, rounding and date conventions with many specific cases.
Coverage is limited to the rules. Database behaviour and the unseen parts of the value layer are not tested here.

terms.meaning: a check in code that stops the program with an error if a statement is false
a short label such as includes AFUDC that records what a stated figure covers

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test file setup
sections.what: Loads the checking tools and the rule functions, and states the command that runs the file. It is the only place the file says how to run it.
sections.why: Likely reason: the file has to import the same rules the app uses so the checks test the real code.
sections.watch_out: If an import path is renamed, every check stops running at once.

sections.name: usd
sections.title: Checks for rounding and value comparison
sections.what: Checks that stated figures such as US$1.3B and 1,232M are compared at the right rounding step. For example, 1,231.7 and 1,232 are treated as the same value, while 1,300 and 1,231.7 are not.
sections.why: Likely reason: source figures are rounded when stated, so a strict comparison would flag false conflicts.
sections.watch_out: The comparison rules decide whether two figures are treated as the same. Changing them changes which values are flagged.

sections.name: mw
sections.title: Checks for units
sections.what: Checks that figures with different units, such as MW and MWe, never match, and that close but different capacities do not match.
sections.why: Likely reason: mixing units would make wrong figures look correct.
sections.watch_out: A unit mismatch is always treated as a difference, so a unit spelling change can create conflicts.

sections.name: r
sections.title: Checks for date conventions
sections.what: Checks that many stated dates resolve to the expected day, and that refused forms such as winter, ranges and wording like later stay unresolved. It also checks that editing a convention changes the result and that restoring the defaults brings it back.
sections.why: Likely reason: the date rules are where the most subtle errors happen, so each covered form has a fixed expected answer.
sections.watch_out: The file changes the shared live conventions during the run and restores them at the end. If it stops early, the restore is skipped.

summary: A test script that checks the value rules: how basis tags are read from text, how numbers are compared with rounding, and how stated dates are resolved under the conventions.
purpose: Catches mistakes in the evidence rules before they reach real project data, so changes to the rules can be trusted.
why: Likely reason: the rules were fixed after a review, and this file keeps those fixes from regressing.
how: It loads the rule functions, runs a long list of checks with assert, changes the conventions for a moment to prove that edits take effect, restores the defaults, prints a success line, and exits. Any failed check stops the script with an error.
inputs: No inputs. It uses the built-in rule functions and default conventions.
outputs: A success message if every check passes, or an error showing the first failing check.
risks: It covers only the rules, not the database. A passing run does not prove the saved data is correct.
debug: Run the file with the command given in its header. If a check fails, the message names the line. Compare the expected text with what the matching rule in metrics.ts, store.ts or dateRules.ts returns.
